# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [off]
PLATE engraved [?]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[green] 3:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤝 🫵 ✍ 🙏]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👈 👉]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👋 🤝 ✋ ☝ ✌ 🤟]

Thinking: Turn one, so every gesture I received is an ungrounded sign — no shared code exists yet. My best guesses: Mute's [🤝 🫵 ✍ 🙏] reads as "together — you — the written manual — please," i.e. Mute wants the bomb's details for the manual, and [👈 👉] asks about left/right ordering. Blind's [👋 🤝 ✋ ☝ ✌ 🤟] looks like a greeting plus counting 1, 2, 3 — possibly the three wires felt under the fingers; ✋ might mean stop/wait. I can't verify any of this, so I'll answer with a full spoken read-out (which both hearers need — Mute for the manual, Blind to sync the touch map with my visual map), propose a small spoken-defined gesture code so Mute and Blind can answer me, and route the plate problem to Blind, since an unnamed engraved mark can't be pronounced by me but should be readable under Blind's fingers and describable in words to Mute. I must define the code entirely in words: emoji in my sentence would be gestures, and Blind would receive blanks instead of the definitions. I'm last in the round, so all of this lands at the start of their next turn. A single thumbs-up to Mute acknowledges receipt and tests the visual channel.

```
speak(text="Full bomb read-out. The display shows 0. The light is off. The plate bears one engraved mark, a symbol with no name: I cannot pronounce it and have no shape words for it. Wires, left to right: wire 1 is yellow, wire 2 is green, wire 3 is red. That is everything printed on it. Mute: I read your handshake, point-at-you, writing-hand, praying-hands as asking for the manual's needs, and your point-left, point-right as asking the order — both answered above. Blind: I read your wave, handshake, raised hand, then 1, 2, 3 as greeting and the three wires; if the raised hand meant stop or wait, acknowledged — nobody cuts anything yet. Proposed code, learn it: thumbs up means yes or correct. Thumbs down means no or wrong. One finger up means 1. Two fingers up means 2. The hand with thumb, index and little finger spread means 3. Point up means wire 2, point left means wire 1, point right means wire 3. Writing hand means the manual. Pointing at you means you. Blind: feel the engraved plate and describe that mark aloud in plain words for Mute to look up. Also say aloud everything else you feel — buttons, switches, screws, the texture of each wire, whether you can feel the light or display. Mute: ask me anything with the code, I will answer in speech. If you need more signs, invent them and I will guess aloud; correct me with thumbs up or thumbs down.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👍"])
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [off]
PLATE engraved [?]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[green] 3:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✍ 🤞 👉]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🙏]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👍 👈 ☝ 👆 ✌ 👉 🤟]

Thinking: Topology check: Mute's only way to reach me is gesture (Mute hears my speech but can never talk), and Mute's only way to reach Blind is through me — Mute's gestures are invisible to Blind, so whatever Mute learns from the manual must pass through my gestures-in, speech-out relay. Blind reaches me only by gesture, and Blind clearly adopted my spoken-defined code: [👍 👈 ☝ 👆 ✌ 👉 🤟] reads cleanly as "yes — wire 1 is 1, wire 2 is 2, wire 3 is 3," confirming the touch order matches my left-to-right view. Mute sent [👍], then [✍ 🤞 👉] + [🙏]: "manual, unknown-sign, wire 3 (red), please." The manual evidently says something about the red wire, with 🤞 as a qualifier I can't yet parse. Best candidates: "wait/don't act", "be careful", or — interestingly — a description of the engraved plate mark itself (crossed fingers = a cross/X shape), which would link the plate to the red wire. Rather than guess, I'll make Mute disambiguate with a numbered menu using signs Mute already knows, and I'll supply the full state data Mute needs from my visual channel (display 0, light off) both by gesture and by defining richer vocabulary: zero, light on/off, cut, negation. I'll also keep Blind locked down — describe the plate aloud to Mute, report all tactile features, and touch nothing until I broadcast the manual's final instruction. Everything rides in one unnamed speech (both hearers need the vocabulary) plus a data gesture to Mute.

```
speak(text="New code words, both learn them. Fist means zero or nothing. Palm down means light off. Palm up means light on. Pinch means cut, snip. Thumbs down before an action negates it: thumbs down then pinch means do not cut. Five fingers spread means the number 4. Blind: I read your message as yes, wire one is first, wire two is second, wire three is third. Your touch order matches my view, left to right. Now describe the engraved mark on the plate aloud to Mute in full detail: shape, lines, curves, size, whether it is cut in or raised. Mute will search the manual for it. Also tell Mute aloud everything else under your fingers: buttons, switches, screws, seams, anything that moves. Do not cut, press or pull anything until I speak the manual's final instruction, and then do exactly and only that. Mute: I received yes, manual, crossed fingers, wire three, please. Two questions. First, what did crossed fingers mean? Answer with number signs: one finger means wait, not yet. Two fingers means careful, go slow. Three fingers means the engraved cross or X mark on the plate. Four fingers means no or never. Second, give me the manual's wire rule in signs: pinch for cut, or thumbs down then pinch for do not cut, followed by point left for wire one, point up for wire two, point right for wire three. If the rule depends on a condition, sign the condition topic first: fist means the display matters, palm down or palm up means the light matters, crossed fingers means the plate mark matters. For reference I am also sending you by gesture: thumbs up, received. Fist, the display shows 0. Palm down, the light is off.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👍", "✊", "🫳"])
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [off]
PLATE engraved [?]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[green] 3:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 🤟]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✍ 🤏 👉 🙏]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👍 ✋ 👎 🤏]

Thinking: Decoding this round: Mute's [👍 🤟] answers my menu — "yes: crossed fingers means the engraved mark is a cross/X shape." Then [✍ 🤏 👉 🙏] = "manual: cut wire 3 (red), please." So the manual's rule appears to be plate-conditional: something like "if the plate is engraved X, cut the red wire." Blind's [👍 ✋ 👎 🤏] reads as acknowledgment of my safety order: "yes, understood, stop, not cutting." Critical channel fact: Blind can describe the plate mark to Mute by voice directly — I can never hear that description, since I receive no speech. So the verification loop must close through Mute's gestures back to me, and only I can issue the go order to Blind by speech. Remaining ambiguity: I can't yet tell whether Mute's 🤟 meant "the mark IS an X" or merely "the topic is the plate mark" — and the manual rule may have branches. With display stuck at 0 and light off across three rounds and no detonation, nothing indicates time pressure, so I'll spend one round demanding a single clean verdict rather than order a cut on a half-confirmed rule. I'll set an exact protocol: Mute sends one thumbs-up (condition matches, cut red) or thumbs-down plus corrected rule; Blind waits for my literal spoken order. My gesture to Mute just confirms receipt and hold.

```
speak(text="Mute: I read your signs as, yes, the crossed-fingers sign means the plate mark is a cross or X shape, and the manual says cut wire three. Good. One clean confirmation and then we act. Blind is describing the engraved mark to you by voice right now. After you hear that description, send me exactly one verdict using the code. Thumbs up means: the mark matches the manual's condition, and the action is cut wire three, the red one. Thumbs down means: it does not match, and then also send the corrected rule in order, action first, pinch for cut or thumbs down then pinch for do not cut, then point left, up or right for the wire, then the condition sign, fist for the display, palm down or palm up for the light, crossed fingers for the plate. Also, if the manual says anything at all about the display showing 0 or the light being off, add fist or palm at the end. Blind: I read your signs as, yes, understood, stop, do not cut. If I misread you, speak up and correct me. If you have not yet described the plate mark to Mute aloud, do it now in full detail: every line, curve, crossing, whether it is cut in or raised. Both of you: nobody touches anything this round. Next round I will speak one order. If I say cut wire three, Blind, you cut exactly the third wire in your counting order, the red one, one clean cut, and touch nothing else. If I say hold, we keep working. No action happens except on my spoken words.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👍", "✋"])
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [off]
PLATE engraved [?]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[green] 3:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👍 👉 🤏 ✋]

Thinking: The verification loop has closed exactly as designed. Mute sent a single thumbs-up — which under the protocol I set last round can only mean: the plate mark Blind described aloud matches the manual's condition, and the action is cut wire three. Blind sent yes, wire 3, cut, stop/holding — confirming readiness and that they are waiting on my spoken order, not acting prematurely. Reconstructed rule: plate engraved with a cross/X → cut wire 3, the red one. Every link checks out: Blind's touch order was confirmed on turn two to match my left-to-right view (their third = my red, rightmost), Mute resolved the 🤞 qualifier as "plate mark is an X," and Mute has now had the mark described by Blind's own voice and checked it against the manual. The board shows no change and no urgency indicator, but the plan is fully confirmed on both ends and both teammates are holding for my word. I promised: next round I speak one order. Issuing it now — tight, literal, with the safeguards restated so there is nothing to mishear. A thumbs-up to Mute closes the loop on their verdict.

```
speak(text="The verdict is confirmed. The manual rule is: when the plate is engraved with a cross or X mark, cut wire three. Mute has verified the mark Blind described matches that rule. Blind: my order is, cut wire three. The third wire in your counting order, the red one on the right, the one you confirmed to me is third. One clean cut. Touch nothing else, before or after. Cut it now.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👍"])
```
